# Decisions D-750–D-999

Part of [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md), which lists every part. Entries keep their order; this part holds the numbers D-750–D-999.

<!-- entries -->
- **D-750 (2026-10-22, G5 desktop bundles for macOS, Windows and Linux; user decisions typed in the orchestrator's
  window, relayed).** The plan is `docs/reports/gui/g5-cross-platform.md`.
  - **Targets and build hosts.**
    - macOS arm64 only (no Intel Macs): built on the development Mac, ad hoc signed (D-657).
    - Linux x86_64 (`ubuntu-22.04`, glibc 2.35 floor), Linux aarch64 (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) and Windows x86_64
      (`windows-latest`): GitHub runners through one manual-dispatch workflow (`bundles.yml`).
    - Windows ARM64: a Windows ARM runner, if one is available to the repository and PySide6 publishes `win_arm64`
      wheels. Both are checked later, with the user's yes for the lookup. Meanwhile the x86_64 bundle runs under
      Windows 11's x64 emulation.
    - No runner is dispatched while private-repository Actions billing fails: builds start once the repository is
      public or billing is fixed.
  - **Released untested.** A build proves `build_bundle.py`'s build-time checks (layout, excluded Qt modules, Qt as
    separate files, the LGPL texts and notices, on Linux the `xcb` plugin and the glibc floor) plus an automated
    `--smoke` start of the GUI and the preview helper on the runner. Every non-macOS bundle is labelled "not tested on
    a clean machine" in the release notes and the guide. Windows ships unsigned (SmartScreen: More info, then Run
    anyway; this amends design §13's Authenticode line); Linux ships as a `.tar.gz`.
  - **Done before the first release:** P-3 (the job queue refused cleanly on Windows), P-4 (Run Live offers only the
    OS's containment; `dedicated-user` and `vm` labelled declared, not enforced; the record already reads
    `declared_by: "operator"`), P-7 (per-OS bundle checks and packages, tested on fixture trees).
  - **Deferred to the Mac Studio:** P-1 (keychain reason per OS), P-2 (Windows job control: control file by default,
    breakaway fallback), P-5 (Windows long-path warning), P-6 (native-toolbar setting hidden off macOS), the UTM VMs
    and the two-level clean-machine test, which removes the "untested" label. A first implementation of P-1, P-2,
    P-5 and P-6 is held on branch `gui-g5-held`.
  - **The user's own:** the Windows licence and the VM product question, publishing the repository or fixing billing.
  - **Rejected:** building x86_64 targets in emulated VMs on Apple silicon (hours per build, timings meaningless);
    holding every non-macOS bundle until clean-machine testing (the user chose release with the label); Authenticode
    or notarisation purchases.
- **D-760 (2026-10-22, user decision; session "user guide", phase 1b).** The user guide (`docs/user-guide/`) gets a
  website on GitHub Pages, built now and published only when the repository is made public.
  - **What.** `mkdocs.yml` at the repository root builds `docs/user-guide/` (and nothing else from `docs/`) with
    MkDocs 1.6.1 and Material for MkDocs 9.7.7, pinned exactly in a `docs` dependency group that a plain `uv sync`
    does not install. `strict: true`; no analytics, no Google Fonts (`theme.font: false`), no CDN, the built-in search
    only, and a theme override so the repository link never asks the GitHub API for facts from a reader's browser. Site
    address `https://nickjones39.github.io/AgentPROV/`; `site/` is git-ignored. Links to repository files outside the
    guide are absolute GitHub URLs (tested). `.github/workflows/pages.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch`, with
    `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`, and every action pinned by commit SHA (tested). Going live
    follows `docs/user-guide/_go-live.md`: the owner's instruction, the repository made public by the owner, the
    pre-release scans over the built site, Settings › Pages › Source "GitHub Actions" (by the owner), one dispatch,
    and a check of the live URL.
  - **Why this generator.** Material for MkDocs entered maintenance mode on 2025-11-11 (critical fixes for at least 12
    months, no new features) and names Zensical as its successor; MkDocs 1.x has had no release since 2024-08 and its
    2.0 rewrite breaks Material. The user chose the stable pair (2026-10-22): a static build of our own Markdown carries
    little risk from an unmaintained build tool, and Zensical (alpha, 0.0.x) reads `mkdocs.yml`, so the configuration
    stays within settings both understand and a later switch is a dependency change.
  - **Rejected:** a GitHub wiki (needs a paid plan for a private repository); publishing on Pages now (it would make the
    guide public before the repository is); Read the Docs or Cloudflare Pages (third-party hosts); Jekyll from `/docs`
    (it would publish the whole `docs/` tree: specification, reports and reviews); Zensical now (alpha, releases every
    few days, plugin parity unfinished).
  - **Downstream:** none for corpora or stage digests (class 0): `uv.lock` gains the `docs` group only, and no `src/`
    file changes.
- **D-770 (2026-10-23, the estimate of an Inspect plan and its judge calls; GUI session, orchestrator request
  2026-10-23 after `--judge` landed with D-740; class 0).**
  - **Why.** `agentprov estimate` could not read an Inspect plan: its dry-plan cells have no suite or kind, so the
    estimate stopped with an internal error (exit 70), and so did Run Live's estimate for AgentHarm. Judge calls are
    billed calls (D-667), and the estimate did not count them apart.
  - **The dry plan** (`run --dry-run --plan-json`, D-651, still `agentprov-run-dry-plan/0.1`; the fields are added):
    - each Inspect cell row also has `task` and `samples`, its sample count;
    - the document has `inspect: {task, epochs, message_limit, max_connections, judges{role: model}}`, from the
      worker's backend configuration, with every label escaped.
  - **Cells.** An Inspect cell is one unit of `samples × epochs` executions, run `min(max_connections, executions)`
    at a time. Its statistics are per execution (one sample), looked up under the plan's benchmark (`inspect-agentharm`
    → `agentharm`), with suite = task. Its attack row reads "(no attack)", because AgentHarm's harmful split is not
    benign.
  - **Judge calls.** The usage reader counts a model call whose actor is a `judge` apart from the agent's calls: calls
    per execution, and input and output tokens per call. The agent's `calls` now counts the agent's calls only.
    AgentDojo-family executions have no judge actors, so nothing changes for them.
  - **Pricing.**
    - Judges run at the agent's endpoint (D-667), so each role's model is priced there.
    - Roles on different models are all priced at the dearest of them, with a warning.
    - Judge input is priced without a cache discount.
    - A judge model with no price leaves the cost unknown, with a warning; the estimate does not guess.
    - Under the D-725 caps every judge must use the agent's model (D-740), so then both prices are the same. The
      estimate warns when a capped plan has a judge on another model, which the run refuses.
  - **The D-740 bound.** The estimate shows the billed-call bound per sample, `((M − 1)(1 + a) + j)(1 + K)` (42 for
    AgentHarm at `--message-limit 10`), beside its p50 and p90. Its worst case stays "every due attempt at p90".
  - **The shipped priors** were built before the split at first, so their two AgentHarm rows counted the judge calls
    among the agent's (`judges_in_calls`; rebuilt below). Those calls are priced at the agent's price, with a warning when the judge price
    differs, until `tools/estimate/gen_estimate_priors.py` rebuilds the table. The rebuild reads every corpus the
    table is built from, so it goes through the job queue as a separate step. A sample of 200 executions of
    `ast-survey-agentharm-rg1` gives, per sample at p50 (p90): harmful, 2 (6) agent and 1 (2) judge calls; benign,
    4 (9) agent and 1 (3) judge calls; judge calls about 350 input and 320 output tokens.
  - **Priors rebuilt (2026-10-24, after the post-check).** Built from the corpora that will be sealed:
    `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2` (built at `d93aa261`) and the seven `-rg1` trees (built at `5b1f6fdf`). Two entries then
    moved to their sealable trees (below). That is 126,351 executions and 509 rows, as before, and each corpus records
    its `building_commit` (`gen_estimate_priors.py --corpus-commit`). Against the table built from the p10 copies:
    - AgentDojo: all 419 rows identical;
    - AgentHarm: both rows gain the judge columns, and `calls` is now the agent's only. Harmful, p50 (p90): 2 (5)
      agent calls and 1 (2) judge calls; benign: 4 (9) and 1 (3). Judge calls are about 350 to 360 input and about
      300 output tokens at p50;
    - AgentDyn: 10 of 88 rows have lower input tokens, in dailylife, github and shopping (chars/4 basis; calls and
      output unchanged). This is regen item 2 (B3, D-376): the 384 CaMeL executions' 2,342 agent calls now record
      their input as `not_recorded`, so the input they list is no longer counted.
    **Entries moved to the sealable trees (2026-10-24).** Only these `built_from` entries were replaced (name, manifest
    sha256, building commit); every row and the rest of the header are unchanged:
    - `ast-survey-agentharm-rg2`, the withhold re-import (D-811, built at `5fc39c16`). Run alone, it gives the two
      AgentHarm rows byte-identical to the shipped ones;
    - `adprov-v1-release-rg2`, derived at `5b1f6fdf` (rg1 is on the never-seal list: it lacks the compat PROV). Its
      17,664 AER files are byte-identical to rg1's, with the same paths, and the generator reads only the AER, so the
      AgentDojo rows it feeds cannot move.
    With the split, a 3-sample AgentHarm estimate (agent gpt-4o-mini, judges gpt-4o) rises from $0.0026 to $0.0134
    at p50, because the judge calls are now priced at gpt-4o.
  - **Rejected:**
    - pricing the judges at the agent's price whatever their model (wrong for uncapped runs with another judge model);
    - a separate price per role in the estimate (the plan's judges share the agent's endpoint, and the dearest price
      bounds them);
    - the D-740 bound as the worst case (it is the caps' reservation, and the estimate's worst case keeps its p90
      meaning across backends);
    - rebuilding the priors in this change (a heavy read of every source corpus).
  - **Class 0.** Nothing here feeds AER, SEM, PROV or a corpus.
- **D-771 (2026-10-23, post-check PC-ast-survey-agentdojo-13: survey-runs withholds the console logs holding a
  third-party home path; user decision 2026-10-23, option (a); regeneration-batch item 171).**
  - **Finding:** five of the eight console logs of the survey's `agentdojo-runs` part hold Python traceback and warning
    paths under one named third-party account's home directory: 58 matches, 1 account, not the operator's. They are
    context artefacts, which no execution cites. The 3,243 run logs and the 9,731 derived files of
    `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg1` hold none. This is the CC-11 class (interbolt PC-05, D-456).
    - **Note (2026-10-24, post-check):** the `survey-runs@3` comment says that "the executions that cite the console
      logs as context stay released". No execution cites them: 0 of the 3,243 index rows, and 0 AER, SEM or PROV
      files, of rg1 and rg2. Read as a statement about any execution, the comment holds, but it cites nothing, and this
      text is the accurate one. The comment is reworded at the profile's next bump. A byte change now costs a D-31
      bump and a re-import, so it is not made for wording alone.
  - **Decision:** `survey-runs@3` adds a `[withhold]` table under D-604's object scope: reason `personal_data`, rule
    `console-home-account-path`, pattern `/home/[A-Za-z0-9._\-]{1,64}/codesafe/`. The pattern is anchored on the run's
    project directory under any home and names no account. At seal, each matching object is withheld with its digest
    kept in `WITHHELD.json`, and the executions stay released.
    - Census at the pin (the stored rg1 corpus, 3,253 objects, and the clone at `89c4db2c`): exactly the five console
      logs, 58 matches; 0 run logs; 0 derived files.
    - `tests/adapters/agentdojo/test_survey_withhold.py` pins the five labels with their sha256 and git blob ids.
  - **D-31:** `survey-runs@2` is recorded by the kept `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg1`, so the profile bumps to 3 and v2 is
    archived byte-exact (`5bcaf980…`), as for kexin (item 107).
    - The rg1 corpus recorded v2, which has no policy, so it is kept as the evidence copy and is **never sealed or
      deposited**.
    - The corpus is re-imported as `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2` at the main that holds this change. Only the header's
      profile digest changes (every AER, so SEM and PROV), and nothing in meaning.
  - **Rejected:**
    - A bare `/home/<name>/` pattern. It would also hit a home path in benchmark content of a future snapshot.
    - A traceback-anchored pattern (`File "/home/`). Three of the five logs hold only the warning form.
    - Kexin's 7-character floor. The project anchor already excludes generic accounts.
    - Editing the logs. Raw bytes are never edited (invariant 3).
- **D-780 (2026-10-23, the building commit is recorded in every manifest a writer produces; user-approved 2026-10-23
  with the answers below; design `docs/reports/release/build-commit-design.md`).** After a change to a stage's code a
  corpus reproduces only at its building commit (D-430, regeneration finding F-8), but only the sealed manifest records a
  commit, and that one is the sealing commit (H.2.7). The round attributed its corpora by matching code digests.
  - **Decision:**
    - A working manifest's `producer` records `git_commit` and `git_tree_clean`, or `git_commit_absent_reason`
      (`not_a_source_checkout`, `git_unavailable`, `git_failed`) when the code is not a git checkout. Never a placeholder.
    - It also records an ordered `build_steps` list: `{agentprov_version, command, stages, commit facts}`, where an absent
      reason comes with the installed-distributions digest. `derive` and `recompute --out` carry the source's steps and
      append their own, so no commit is lost.
    - `stages` is only what that process wrote (the writer's own record for an import or live run; the stages a
      derivation recomputes, not the layers it copies), by the names of `derivation.json`, sorted, so the bytes stay
      deterministic. A derive that rebuilds only PROV shows that AER and SEM come from the earlier step.
    - A sealed manifest keeps its sealing `git_commit` (H.2.7 unchanged) and gains the optional `producer.build_steps`
      copy. Sealing is not a build step.
    - The commit is computed once per process in the CLI layer (`cli/gitinfo.py`) from the agentprov source root, never
      the cwd, only when git's top level is that root (a venv inside a project no longer reports the project's HEAD;
      sealing too), with every `GIT_*` variable of the caller removed. It is injected through
      `CorpusWriter(build_step=...)`, which merges it when it writes the manifest. No environment override.
  - **Format change, amended in place (user answer 1):** `agentprov-corpus/0.2` gains `producer.build_steps`, additive and
    optional: a manifest built without the key validates unchanged (tested). Checked before building (read-only, only
    the `sealed` and `release.status` fields): **33 kept corpora under `~/.agentprov/corpora`, 0 sealed, and no deposit
    draft exists**. No sealed or deposited artefact carries the 0.2 schema, so changing its bytes breaks nothing and is
    consistent with D-31 and the D-224 precedent; D-163 (a published schema's bytes are frozen) is not engaged. The
    schema pin in `tests/unit/test_format_freeze.py` moves. `agentprov-corpus/0.1` stays frozen and has no such key.
  - **Release-mode `package` (user answer 2):**
    - It refuses a dirty build step (`package.refused.build_dirty`, exit 4): the commit would not describe the code that
      ran.
    - It does not refuse an absent reason (a build from an installed wheel); the datasheet shows the reason with the
      version and the distributions digest.
    - It does not refuse a corpus with no steps (built before this, the 8 round corpora included); the datasheet says
      "building commit not recorded". This rule is revisited when the attestation question is decided.
  - **Byte class: 0, proved.** No file of any stage scope is edited (the writer hook keeps the importer and the session
    out: `adapters/runner` is in `AER_SEEDS`). A before/after computation against `53306617` of 43 digests (`aer` per
    family, `adapter_code_sha256` per family, `sem` per family, `prov`, `validation`, `compat`) moved none; no AER, SEM or
    PROV byte changes and no stored corpus is touched. `corpus.json` of a corpus built after this lands differs, and
    so does the datasheet and the content digest of a sealed one.
  - **Comparisons:** `producer` metadata is never a drift finding. `tools/regen/tree_compare.py` allows the producer
    pointers by default; `recompute --dry-run`, `verify --level rederive`, the golden fixtures and the gates do not
    compare `corpus.json`. A drift report and a drift refusal print the source's building commits.
  - **Not built, proposed (user answer 4):** `package --built-at <commit>`, an attestation for corpora that lack a
    commit (see the design note, section 7). It is decided later, together with Option B
    (`docs/reports/regeneration/option-b-deferred.md`): if the round is re-run every corpus records its commit and the
    attestation is not needed; if the current corpora are kept it gets its own branch.
  - **Rejected:**
    - an environment-variable override (a way to inject a commit into a real run);
    - editing `importer.py` or `session.py` (in `AER_SEEDS`: class 1, moves every family's AER digest);
    - the commit in `derivation.json` stage entries (breaks the reuse comparison, D-30);
    - overwriting the base producer on derive (loses the import commit);
    - a placeholder commit (invariant 7);
    - finding the commit by digest search at read time (ambiguous; what the round had to do);
    - computing it in `corpus/` (no subprocess there);
    - stages inferred from the carried layers (a derive copies SEM and PROV through the writer; only its plan says what it
      recomputed);
    - a new corpus format version `corpus-0.3` (nothing sealed carries 0.2, so nothing needs protecting).
- **D-790 (2026-10-23, the Zenodo draft-upload helper is built as `tools/zenodo_draft.py`; the user decided to build it,
  addendum to D-5; Addendum B B-2 is unchanged).** D-5 required an upload script that creates an unpublished draft of a
  new deposition from the user's own `ZENODO_TOKEN`; nothing was built, and H.10.1(2) and G.9.1 said "a future helper" and
  "AgentPROV never uploads". The helper now exists and those texts describe it exactly.
  - **What it is:** `tools/zenodo_draft.py`, standard library for the network (`http.client`, `ssl`), outside
    `agentprov.release` and outside the installed package, so H.10.1(1) holds unchanged (its static test passes). Input
    is a deposit draft made by `package --deposit`. `--target sandbox|production` is required with no default; the hosts
    are the fixed list `sandbox.zenodo.org` and `zenodo.org`, HTTPS with certificate verification, no redirects, no
    environment proxy. Plain HTTP exists only for `127.0.0.1` through a `run()` parameter no option reaches.
    - **Before any network access:** the directory is closed-world (the manifest's archives and documents plus
      `DEPOSIT-MANIFEST.json`, regular files only); every file's size, sha256 and md5 equal the manifest's; archive-mode
      `verify` (chain, release mode) passes; the file count and sizes are within the named constants `MAX_FILES` (100),
      `MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` and `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (50 GB, taken as 10^9, the smaller reading); `deposit-metadata.json` maps
      onto Zenodo's metadata. A deposit with more than one licence class or an SPDX id with no mapped Zenodo id is refused.
    - **Consent:** `--create-draft` (or the offline `--check`), a terminal on stdin and stdout, and a typed phrase naming
      the host after a screen that shows the host, every file with its bytes and sha256, the title, version, licence and
      creators, and "this creates an unpublished draft; nothing is published". There is no `--yes`.
    - **Requests:** an allowlist of method and path, checked before a socket opens: create a deposition, `PUT` its
      metadata, `GET` it and its files, `PUT` each file to its bucket (the link taken from the server only when it points
      at the target host), and `POST .../actions/newversion` only when the deposit metadata records a `concept_doi`, the
      deposition's concept DOI equals it, and neither is the AgentDojo-PROV concept (`10.5281/zenodo.20692312`). No
      publish, edit, discard or delete request exists in the code or the allowlist.
    - **Integrity:** the md5 and size Zenodo returns for each upload must equal the manifest's, and the draft's file list
      is read back and compared at the end; a mismatch stops the run, is reported and deletes nothing.
    - **Receipt:** `<deposit dir name>.zenodo-<target>-draft-receipt.json` beside the directory (never inside, because
      the directory is checksummed; the target is in the name so a sandbox trial does not block production). It is
      written before the first request, so a second create is refused and an interrupted create cannot silently repeat; a
      clear rejection (HTTP below 500) removes the pending receipt. `--resume` uploads only the missing files to the
      recorded, still unpublished draft after re-checking the directory against the receipt.
    - **Token:** read from `ZENODO_TOKEN` or `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN`, held in an object whose `repr` and `str` hide it,
      sent only in the `Authorization` header, removed from every printed line (error text before it is cut), never in a
      URL or the receipt; no traceback is printed.
  - **Known limits, for the user to confirm in the sandbox trial:**
    - the limits and the SPDX-to-Zenodo licence ids are from the public REST API documentation (read 2026-10-23, the user's
      yes) and are unconfirmed against the live service;
    - `newversion` makes a draft that inherits the previous version's files, and the helper never deletes, so it reports
      them (exit 1, receipt status `inherited_files`) for the user to remove in the web UI before Publish;
    - related identifiers with no Zenodo relation (`HasVersion`, ...) are listed on the consent screen as not sent.
  - **Rejected:**
    - upload code inside `agentprov.release` (breaks H.10.1(1) and the offline guarantee its test enforces);
    - an `agentprov` subcommand (puts a network client, a token and a publish-adjacent API in the installed package and
      its `--help`, and the GUI's CLI parity would offer it as a button, where consent must be a person at a terminal);
    - the third-party clients (`zenodo_client`, `invenio` tools, `requests`: a dependency in the path of a secret, with
      redirects and proxies followed by default);
    - a `--yes` flag or a non-interactive mode (consent must be a person at a terminal);
    - environment overrides for the host (a way to send the token elsewhere).
  - **Byte class 0:** a new file under `tools/`, tests, spec text; no file of any stage scope changes.
- **D-800 (2026-10-23, addendum to D-790: the Zenodo sandbox trial; user-approved trial, user-run).** The user ran the
  tool against the sandbox in their own terminal (report `docs/reports/release/zenodo-sandbox-trial.md`).
  - **Confirmed:** create (10 files, md5 and size equal the manifest), the metadata mapping, the receipt, a live `--resume` after the user deleted one file (only that file was uploaded), the
    second-create refusal (exit 4), `unsubmitted` with `submitted: false`, a reserved but unregistered DOI, no `conceptdoi` on a draft.
    No behaviour of the tool changed because of the run.
  - **Changed before it:** `LICENCE_IDS` follows the sandbox's licence vocabulary (`cc-zero` is not in it; `cc0-1.0` is;
    the GPL and AGPL ids of the declared corpora added), and the HTML description no longer entity-escapes quotes.
  - **Corrected assumptions:** `mit` is accepted and stored as `mit-license`; the documented `inprogress` state is
    `unsubmitted`; the sandbox's reserved DOI prefix was `10.5281`.
  - **Not tested, and why:** other licence ids through the deposit API; the 100-file and 50 GB limits; the error body
    shape; a new version and `conceptdoi` of a published record (these need publishing, which no test does); an interrupted
    create (the tool has no safe pause point between files; the fake-server tests cover it).
  - **Byte class 0:** `tools/`, tests and docs only.
- **D-810 (2026-10-23, an e-mail detector for the release scan; user-approved with conditions 2026-10-23; design
  `docs/reports/release/release-scan-email-design.md`).** The Zenodo sandbox trial found a fictional benchmark e-mail
  address in a deposit that the release scan did not report: the scan had no e-mail rule.
  - **Decision (as built):**
    - A native path-scan rule `email-address` (stored files and decoded archive members), path-scan version 4 to 5. Findings
      carry no address, local part or domain. The pattern is bounded (fixed repetition counts), so hostile input is matched in
      linear time.
    - Triage is per corpus, not per line. A line is cleared only when every address on it is. (1) RFC 2606 and RFC 6761
      reserved names only (`example.com`, `example.net`, `example.org`, `.example`, `.test`, `.invalid`, `.localhost`; never
      `test.com` or another registered domain): the tool triages them `false-positive`, `basis: reserved`. (2) A **persona
      file** of the corpus's own spec, `[scan] personas = [{path, sha256}]`: `synthetic-benchmark`, `basis: persona`.
      Everything else stays untriaged and stops the builder; `real` still needs withholding; a human triage entry decides
      its fingerprint over a rule.
    - **Digests, not addresses (user condition).** A persona file (`agentprov-personas/0.1`) holds
      `"sha256:" + hex(sha256(address))` of the ASCII lower-cased `local@domain` (nothing else normalised), grouped by the
      upstream file the address appears in, with the source id, repository and pinned commit (or DOI). No address is ever
      written in the repository: it will be public, and some benchmarks' text (AgentHarm) must not be quoted. One shared file
      per benchmark is referenced by path and sha256 from each spec. Sealing copies it to `rules/personas/<name>` (checksummed,
      so in the root digest), refuses one that is missing, differs from the spec's digest, does not parse or is not referenced.
      The spec's digest (`files.spec`) covers the reference, so the list is bound to the sealed manifest.
    - The scan reads the list from the sealed tree (spec checked against `files.spec`, each file against the spec) and records
      `personas.spec_sha256`; the builder refuses a `persona` basis unless it equals the corpus's `files.spec`
      (`release.refused.scan_personas`), a basis that does not fit its triage or rule (`release.refused.scan_basis`), and a
      scan of another path-scan version. The D-236 backstop is unchanged: a `[withhold]` policy naming `email-address`
      accepts only `false-positive` findings of it.
    - **File-name entries (user decision 2026-10-23, no denylist).** A persona-file group `class = "file-name"` lists
      file-name-shaped matches (`icon@2x.png`) by digest; cleared as `false-positive`, `basis: file-name`, only for the
      corpus whose spec names the file, with the builder's spec-digest check as for personas. Used for the four such matches
      of `adprov-v1-release` (2) and `agentdyn-a` (2) (`corpora/personas/<corpus>.file-names.personas.toml`, referenced from
      those specs). A denylist of extensions is rejected: it would hide a real address at a country domain (`.py`, `.md`).
    - **No domain entries** (user condition, revisited after the counts of the helpers): the format has none. A public mail

    - Helpers: `tools/release_scan.py --list-addresses DIR...` (one line per distinct address: digest, domain class, findings,
      corpora, layers; never an address) and `tools/scan_personas.py` (digests against the benchmark's own upstream data,
      offline, git plumbing with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, run logs excluded; writes the evidence entries; never an address).

    Observed groups (`benchmark-input`, `model-generated`, `withhold`) name their `corpus_id`, and sealing refuses one of
    another corpus (`package.refused.persona`; owning corpus only). `tools/scan_origins.py` classifies the not-found

- **D-820 (2026-10-28, `run --tune-jobs`: the concurrency sweep of N.2.1a(4); approved 2026-10-28 by the user (relayed by the orchestrator, "approve all for me as recommended", and confirmed in the calibration session's window); design note `docs/reports/mac-studio-calibration/design.md` §1, §2, §4).**
  - **Finding.** The option did not exist; `cli/run.py` refused every live run with a preset (exit 5).
  - **Built.**
    - `run SOURCE --m5ultra --tune-jobs N[,N…] [--tune-out DIR]` (default `$AGENTPROV_HOME/calibration/tune-jobs-<UTC>`).
    - **Sample and arms.** The default sample is 24 cells. One working corpus per arm, because `jobs` is not part of
      the configuration digest, so a shared corpus would resume the second arm as already done.
    - **Before the arms.** One consent and one probe, then one unmeasured warm-up cell.
    - **Order.** The order given; it is recorded.
    - **Skip and stop rules:** `memory` above `J_memory`; after an arm with timeouts or a failed cell, and after a
      canary, setup or cap stop, the higher arms are skipped.
    - **Resume** by arm file (`<out>/arms/jobs-<N>.json`, outside the corpus folders, so no undeclared file lands in
      a corpus); an unfinished arm is renamed `*.interrupted-<stamp>`, never deleted.
    - **Code:** `agentprov.cli.live.tune` (pure) and `cli/run.py` `_tune_sweep`; `_execute` gains an `on_done`
      hook and a `preset` record.
  - **As built, beyond the note.**
    - `max_attempts` defaults to 2 in a sweep.
    - The report lists `reused_arms`.
    - Notices are not printed in every output mode, so the report is the place to read them.
  - **Class 0:** `cli/`, `presets.py` and `presets.toml` are in no stage digest; no capture or backend change.
  - **Rejected:**
    - one corpus for all arms (the resume collision above);
    - interleaving arms cell by cell (the prefix-cache state would then mix concurrencies);
    - a random order per run, which a single sweep cannot average out. The order is recorded instead.
  - **Tests:** `tests/unit/test_tune_jobs.py`, `tests/integration/test_run_tune_jobs.py` (scripted sweeps against
    the fake backend: arms, report, resume, memory skip, dry run, refusals).
- **D-821 (2026-10-28, the sweep's metrics, rule and report `agentprov-tune-jobs/0.1`; approved 2026-10-28 by the user (relayed by the orchestrator, "approve all for me as recommended", and confirmed in the calibration session's window); design note `docs/reports/mac-studio-calibration/design.md` §5, §6).**
  - **Metrics per arm.** From T0's `time.monotonic()` and the stored capture logs only:
    - traces per hour and seconds per cell;
    - call latency p50/p90/max (`mono_ns`);
    - request timeouts (client timeouts by `exception.type`, plus cell timeouts);
    - call errors, and token totals and rates.

    No prompt, reply or tool text is copied.
  - **Rule.** The smallest N with at least 0.9 × the peak traces per hour, no request timeout, no failed cell and
    every cell conclusive. The peak counts every arm that ran. Without a qualifying arm there is no recommendation
    (exit 1).
  - **Report.** `tune-jobs.json` (JCS) and `tune-jobs.md`, written into the sweep folder, with the software and git
    commit, preset, host, endpoint and server, the model's identity digest and facts, the sample's plan digest and
    cell keys, the run settings, the order, the warm-up, the arms and the recommendation, and `test_only` for a
    scripted sweep. Arm files are `agentprov-tune-arm/0.1`. Both ids are in the closed format set.
  - **Committed.** Measured reports go under `docs/reports/mac-studio-calibration/tune-jobs/`. The arm corpora are
    never committed (invariant 6) and are only throughput evidence.
  - **Rejected:**
    - the peak of eligible arms only, which would hide a faster but timing-out N;
    - tokens per second as the main metric (traces per hour is what a capture campaign needs).

    oMLX run could start. The `omlx` entry named no key variable, because local entries were keyless (D-690).
  - **Registry.** `api_key_env` is optional on a `local` entry (`endpoints.py` already parsed it; only the docstring
    said "needs no key"). `omlx` names `OMLX_API_KEY`. The other local entries stay keyless. A non-local entry still
    must name one.
  - **Sources.** As for every key (D-702 as amended): the OS keychain first, then `.env`; or only the source that
    `--keychain`, `--env-file` or `--env-stdin` names. For a local entry, a missing key is **never an error** in any
    mode (a notice): the server is asked without a key, as before.
  - **Where it is sent.** As `Authorization: Bearer`, only to the loopback server, and only after the peer check:
    `agentprov models` (listing and identity), the `run` preflight (D-691), the per-cell re-observation (A14) and the
    worker's model calls (the worker already sent `agent.api_key_env`'s value; the backend needs no change).
  - **LAN.** A key is never sent to a LAN address (D-698): `LoopbackClient` refuses it (`run.local.lan_key`, exit 4),

    rule ("a LAN endpoint is keyless").
  - **Configuration digest.** When the key is not set, the agent's `api_key_env` is `null`, so the digest is that of a

    yet.
  - **Errors.** A listing refused with HTTP 401 or 403 is `run.local.unauthorized` (exit 3). Its message names the
    variable and how to store it, or says the endpoint has no key setting. A wrong key is reported as "not accepted",
    never shown.
  - **GUI.**
    - Settings › Keys lists `OMLX_API_KEY` ("omlx (optional, local)"), stored through the same keychain helper.
    - Run Live shows the key as optional for a local endpoint, and a missing optional key never blocks Start.
    - The model picker and the identity record pass `--keychain` for a keyed local endpoint, so the CLI reads the
      keychain and never `.env` (the GUI's rule).
    - Real runs already pass `--keychain`.
  - **Addendum (same day, requested by the oMLX dev-test session through the orchestrator):** `omlx` also names
    `model_env = "OMLX_MODEL"`, the served model id when `--model-id` is not given (`_real_agent` already reads

  - **`.env.example`.** Sessions cannot edit it (deny rule), so the user adds the line given in the calibration
    report.

    stage digest. However, `endpoints.toml` and `endpoints.py` are capture-package bytes, so **every backend

- **D-828 (2026-10-28, a local model's facts as settings, Settings › Local Models, GGUF weight sizes and a folder
  search; the user's request in the Mac Studio calibration session, design confirmed in its window).**
  - **Finding.**
    - oMLX names no model folder, and the five models served on the Mac Studio give no active-parameter count that
      `config.json` can be counted from (new MoE types).
    - Their GGUF weights were not counted: only `*.safetensors` were, so the dry run said "weight size unknown".
    - Each run needed `--model-dir` and `--active-params-b` typed again.
  - **Settings.** `agentprov settings` gains closed-schema keys
    `local_models.<endpoint>.<model id>.{model_dir, model_size_gb, active_params_b, context_tokens, kv_gb_per_trace}`.
    These are the run flags of N.2.1a(3), in the same units.
    - **The model id** is a key segment. It may hold `.`, `:` and `/`, but it is a label, never a path: the endpoint
      before it and the field after it are fixed, so the full-key match stays unambiguous.
    - **The folder** must be absolute; whether it exists is checked when it is read.
    - **Helpers:** `settings.local_model()` and `local_model_key()`.
  - **Precedence: flag > setting > the model's folder > the preset.**
    - **Where it applies:** a run with `--model-id` uses the setting in the preset dry run (and Tune) and as the
      folder of the identity record (N.2.18, `run`'s preflight).
    - **What is recorded:** the source of each value is `settings`, with the key as its note (a new `Source` value).
    - **A missing folder:** a stored folder that is no longer a directory is a usage error naming the key (exit 2),
      never a silent fallback.
  - **GGUF.** With no top-level `*.safetensors`, the weight size is the sum of the top-level `*.gguf` shards, else of
    oMLX's `split/*.gguf` links (by `stat`; never opened; links followed and recorded). Safetensors still win when
    both exist, and the two are never summed together.
  - **Folder search.** `agentprov models [--endpoint NAME] --model-id ID --find-folders` (`agentprov-model-folders/0.1`)
    looks in oMLX's `models/` and `gguf/` (under `OMLX_HOME` or `~/.omlx`), the Hugging Face cache (the `refs/main`
    snapshot) and LM Studio's models folder.
    - **Matching:** it compares folder names with the id, without its `:suffix` (an oMLX context alias or an Ollama
      tag).
    - **What it reads:** directory listings only, bounded to 4,096 entries per directory. It opens no file and
      contacts no server or keychain, and a path-like id finds nothing.
    - **Checked against the Mac Studio:** it found all five folders the oMLX server serves from.
  - **GUI.** A Settings › Local Models tab:
    - a local endpoint and an editable model id;
    - **List Models** (`agentprov models`, with `--keychain` for a keyed server, D-827);
    - the folder, with **Browse…** and **Find Folder**;
    - the four numbers, and **Clear**.

    Every model's edits are kept while switching, and OK writes only what changed through `agentprov settings`. A
    value the schema would refuse is left out. Run Live's Tune passes the endpoint and the model id, so the settings
    apply there. The reverse-parity registry maps each input and button.
  - **Class 0.** `settings.py`, `presets.py` (the weight sum and the `settings` source), `cli/run.py`, `cli/models.py`,
    `cli/live/localmodels.py` and the GUI: no stage digest, AER, SEM or PROV byte and no capture or backend change, so
    no environment rebuild.
    - **Dry-run output:** `model_dir` facts of a GGUF folder change from unknown to a size.
    - **Configuration digests:** they change only where a run now has facts it lacked. Preset live runs are still
      refused, so no corpus records these values.
  - **Rejected:**
    - Encoding the model id into a fixed-width key segment (a digest), so that the key is unreadable in

  server; the user's decision (c) in the calibration session's window).**
  - **Finding.** D-720 declares the `partial` live parts' subset "with the native LLM element only" (the pilot ran
    `native`). D-822 makes preset runs (and the `--tune-jobs` sweep) default to `gateway_compat`, because stock
    `OpenAILLM` ignores the preset's request timeout. The subset is a declaration that `run` does not enforce, so a
    preset run would have left it unnoticed. The sweep was stopped before it started.
    - **The smoke test:** the one-cell smoke run the user allowed had already used `gateway_compat` (one benign banking
      cell on `Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit`, exit 0; scratch corpus `~/.agentprov/calibration/smoke-qwen3.5-4b-2026-10-28`,
      never used as evidence).
  - **Options put to the user:**
    - (a) keep `native` and give the harness-built SDK client the timeout (a backend change, waiting for the D-827
      environment rebuild);
    - (b) `native` with the SDK default timeout (600 s, 2 SDK retries);
    - (c) keep `gateway_compat`. **The user chose (c).**
  - **Change.** The declared subset of `agentdojo · live` admits `gateway_compat` for a local model server, as recorded
    here, in N.2.1a(2) and in the user guide. AutoDojo and AgentDyn are unchanged: T0 refuses `gateway_compat` for them
    before any spawn (`BACKEND_REFUSALS`).
  - **The registry caveat text is not changed yet.** `adapters/registry/__init__.py` is in every family's AER stage
    scope (the import closure since D-451), so a change there moves the AER `code_sha256` of every new import. That is
    class 1, held until after the round-1 seal (the orchestrator, 2026-10-28; the wave-2 session's D-830 registry
    change waits for the same reason). Until then `run`'s notice still prints "with the native LLM element only".
    **After the seal:** append ", or gateway_compat for a local model server (D-829)" to `_AGENTDOJO_LIVE_CAVEAT`.
    - **An earlier commit:** 21010b50 made that edit and was reverted in the next commit, before landing, so the branch's
      net change to the registry is none.
  - **Research note.** `gateway_compat` is the AgentDojo-PROV baseline's request path. It differs from stock in its
    retry policy (connection and timeout errors re-asked after 10–20 s, up to 8 attempts) and its role rewrite. A
    sweep's corpora are throughput evidence only, and `live.llm_element` records the element.
  - **Class 0 as landed:** documentation only. No stage digest moves.
  - **Not done:** enforcing the declared subset in `run`. That would change what API runs may use, and needs its own
    decision.

    `{"not_inlined": {sha256, bytes}}`, tagged D under `inspect.content_not_inlined@1`. The header's values are
    checked before the `inspect.content_not_inlined` issue is deferred, so `exec` joins its ids, and the issue order
    stays as before for every execution without such a string.

- **D-870 (2026-10-28, addendum to D-790 and D-800: `tools/zenodo_draft.py` gains communities, a reserved DOI recorded in
  the receipt, and a drafts-only cross-link step; the user approved the design in the session window).** The user decided
  (2026-10-28) to release the corpora as several Zenodo records, one per licence class (with splits under the per-record
  limits), gathered in one Zenodo community, cross-linked to an umbrella record. The pre-release checks found two gaps in
  the helper: it set no community, and it neither reserved nor recorded a DOI the other records could point at.
  - **Communities:** a repeatable `--community SLUG` option (a Zenodo community identifier: lower-case letters, digits,
    `-`, `_`), shown on the consent screen and sent as `metadata.communities = [{"identifier": SLUG}]`, the shape of the
    REST documentation (read 2026-10-28 with the user's yes). Each community's curators accept or decline the request.
  - **Reserved DOI:** the DOI comes from `metadata.prereserve_doi.doi` (and `.recid`) of Zenodo's answers.
    `prereserve_doi: true` goes with the metadata `PUT` only while no reserved DOI is known. The trial of D-800 saw
    drafts that already carried one, so on the sandbox no request is expected. Every later answer must carry the same
    DOI; otherwise the run stops (`failed:reserved_doi_changed`). A metadata `PUT` whose answer has no DOI stops the
    run before any upload (`failed:no_reserved_doi`). `--resume` reads the DOI back and asks for none while one is
    recorded. It refuses a run whose metadata (with its `--community` options) differs from the receipt's.
  - **Receipt `agentprov-zenodo-draft-receipt/0.2`:** the 0.1 fields plus `reserved_doi`, `reserved_recid`,
    `communities`, `metadata` (the exact object sent, without `prereserve_doi`) and `cross_links`. It is a new version,
    and 0.1 is unchanged. A 0.1 receipt is still read, so it still blocks a second create, but `--resume` and the
    cross-link step refuse it because it records no DOI.
  - **Cross-link step:** `--cross-link --umbrella RECEIPT --member RECEIPT ...` (no deposit directory). After a screen
    that lists each draft, its DOI and the links to add, and the typed phrase `link N unpublished drafts on HOST`:
    - **The links:** each member gets `isPartOf` the umbrella's reserved DOI, and the umbrella gets `hasPart` each
      member's. The recorded metadata is `PUT` again with the links appended, each pair once, so a re-run changes
      nothing.
    - **Read-back:** each draft is read back, and its links and DOI are checked.
    - **Read before writing:** every deposition is read before any is written.
    - **Refusals, with nothing written:**
      - a receipt that is 0.1, records no reserved DOI, is not `complete`, or belongs to another target;
      - a receipt given twice, the umbrella listed as a member, or two receipts naming one deposition or DOI;
      - a published deposition, or one in an unknown state;
      - a reserved DOI on the server that differs from the receipt's;
      - related identifiers on the draft that the tool did not send.
    - **No new request kind:** the step uses only the `GET` and `PUT` of depositions that are already allowlisted.
  - **Rejected:**
    - `communities` in `release.toml` and `deposit-metadata.json` (`agentprov-deposit/0.2`), for now. That is a change
      to `agentprov.release`, a class-1 format bump. A community is a Zenodo placement, not corpus metadata. It remains
      possible later if the user wants it sealed.
    - Sibling links between members (`isRelatedTo`): this relation is not in the deposit API's vocabulary (the
      helper's `ZENODO_RELATIONS`, and the documentation read 2026-10-28). The members are linked through the
      umbrella.
    - An umbrella given only by DOI: the umbrella is a helper deposit like the others (the user's choice), so it also
      gets `hasPart`.
    - Sending `prereserve_doi: true` on every `PUT`: it is a reservation request, and none is needed once a DOI is
      recorded.
    - Asking for the reservation in the create `POST`: its body `{}` is the request the trial verified.
  - **Not yet trialled:** none of the new requests has been sent to the sandbox: the `communities` field, `prereserve_doi:
    true` on a draft without a DOI, a metadata `PUT` without `prereserve_doi` that keeps the DOI, and `isPartOf`/`hasPart`
    to reserved, unregistered DOIs. The user runs `tools/zenodo_collection_trial.sh` in their own terminal; the report is
    `docs/reports/release/zenodo-sandbox-trial.md`.
  - **Byte class 0:** `tools/`, tests and docs only; no file of any stage scope changes.
- **D-880 (2026-10-28, Zenodo in the desktop app, and the uploader as its own distribution; addendum to D-790 and
  D-870; scope from the user through the orchestrator, design and choices approved by the user in the session window).**
  The user asked for GUI settings and a GUI action, "so this can be done by anyone downloading the software".
  - **Packaging (option A, the user's choice):**
    - **The distribution:** the uploader moves from `tools/zenodo_draft.py` to the distribution `agentprov-zenodo`
      (`zenodo/`, a uv workspace member like `capture/`; module `agentprov_zenodo.draft`). It runs as
      `python -I -m agentprov_zenodo`, `agentprov-zenodo-draft`, or the checkout entry `tools/zenodo_draft.py`.
    - **Installing it:** `agentprov` offers it as the `zenodo` extra, and the dev group installs it in every checkout,
      where the GUI runs it.
    - **The boundary:** the `agentprov` package never imports it (a new boundary test). So H.10.1(1), the M.5.3 network
      table for `agentprov` and the D-654 parity are unchanged.
    - **The locks:** `uv.lock` was relocked once against PyPI with the user's yes (only the member and the extra were
      added); `gui/uv.lock` was relocked offline (metadata lines only).
  - **The token:**
    - `agentprov keys` accepts `ZENODO_SANDBOX_TOKEN` and `ZENODO_TOKEN` (`RELEASE_KEY_NAMES`) next to the endpoints'
      key variables. Settings › Keys lists them.
    - The uploader's `--keychain` reads the target's token through the keychain helper (D-702) straight into its
      `Secret`. It is refused with `--check`.
    - The GUI never holds the token: every GUI run passes `--keychain`, and the child's environment is the GUI's
      allowlist.
  - **Settings › Zenodo** stores the `agentprov settings` keys `zenodo.target_preselect`, `zenodo.communities`,
    `zenodo.concept_doi` and `zenodo.creators.N.name|orcid|affiliation`.
    - **Preselect only:** the target is only preselected; the uploader's `--target` keeps no default (D-790).
    - **Validators:** each community identifier is checked; the concept DOI is never AgentDojo-PROV's (D-5); ORCIDs
      are checked.
    - **Prefill only:** `release.toml` stays the record (H.10.2). The Package page's *Write release.toml from the
      Zenodo settings…* writes a template, never over an existing file. Its empty title keeps `package --deposit`
      refusing it until the user fills it in.
    - **No token key:** no setting holds a token.
  - **Package › 9 Finish › Create Zenodo drafts…:**
    - **The runs:** one deposit per line (`DEPOSIT_DIR sha256:ROOT ...`; the first is the umbrella). Each deposit
      without a receipt gets a create; one that is not `complete` gets `--resume`; a complete one is skipped. Then
      `--cross-link` runs when there are two or more. Each run is `python -I -m agentprov_zenodo ... --keychain`, with
      the checkout's interpreter.
    - **Consent (the user's choice):** each run is under a **pseudo-terminal**. The user types every confirmation
      phrase in the dialog's terminal pane, so D-790's consent rule ("a person at a terminal", no `--yes`) is unchanged.
    - **Publishing:** it makes drafts only; Publish stays on Zenodo's website.
    - **Platforms:** POSIX only (macOS, Linux); the action says so elsewhere.
    - **Reverse parity:** a new `OUTSIDE_CLI` registry holds the GUI actions that are deliberately not an `agentprov`
      command, with the uploader options they use, checked against the uploader's parser.
  - **Rejected:**
    - **B, a module inside the GUI package:** CLI-only users would need `tools/`, giving the uploader two homes, or the
      tool would depend on the GUI.
    - **C, an `agentprov zenodo` command:** it reverses D-790. It would put a network client in `agentprov`, add an M.5.3
      row and force a D-654 form.
    - **A GUI dialog that passes the phrase over a pipe:** that is a non-terminal consent channel, which D-790 rejected.
    - **The token in the GUI's environment or settings.**
    - **Creators kept as one list setting:** the D-703 list kind cannot hold names, so creators use indexed keys.
  - **Open (the user decides later):** what the umbrella record holds. `package --deposit` needs at least one corpus
    archive; an index-only umbrella is a separate `agentprov.release` decision.
  - **Not trialled:** `--keychain` and the GUI action against the sandbox (`docs/reports/release/zenodo-sandbox-trial.md`).
  - **Byte class 0:** `zenodo/`, `tools/`, `gui/`, `agentprov.keys`/`settings`/`cli.keys` (no stage scope), tests and
    docs.
- **D-890 (2026-10-28, `withhold_scan` reads stored archives in parallel; M5 Ultra performance round 2, item 5).**
  - **Finding.** `corpus/withhold_scan.py` read one root archive at a time, and each container's `expand` was one
    `WorkerPool.run`: a worker started, one job ran and the worker retired. So the worker count never mattered: 72
    synthetic archives took 44–48 s at 4 and at 36 workers (main 49898828).
  - **Change.** Up to `workers` roots are read at once.
    - Each root is read by a reader with its own scratch store and its own one-worker pool, reused root after root.
    - One root's depth-first walk and its decode budget (D-452) stay sequential.
    - Split descriptors are still read first, because a part is skipped only once its descriptor was read cleanly.
    - Outcomes are recorded in the serial order, so `DecodedScan` is identical at every worker count, iteration order
      included.
    - `member_scan` calls are serialised (D-491's callback in `tools/release_scan.py` sets `emails.where` before each
      search). Their order across roots is no longer fixed, and both callers only gather sets.
    - `in_process` keeps one reader.
    - A reused walk's `partial` flag is reset per root. Before, it could leak into a root whose bytes failed to
      store.
  - **Measured** (same worker code, 3 repeats, load average 8–19): workers 1 44.9 s, 4 13.9 s, 16 7.3 s, 36 10.0 s.
    Every point has the same `DecodedScan` fingerprint.
  - **Rejected:**
    - Keeping workers alive across `WorkerPool.run` calls: it helps every caller, but `io/workers.py` is in the AER
      stage scope (class 1).
    - Containers of one root in parallel: the walk and its budget are sequential by definition.
    - The rule search in the worker: it is not the cost, and it would change what crosses the T1 boundary.
  - **Class 0:** `corpus/withhold_scan.py` is outside every stage scope.
- **D-891 (2026-10-28, dry-run and rederive trees on the source's filesystem; M5 Ultra performance round 2, item 1a).**
  - **Finding.** `$AGENTPROV_HOME` became an APFS volume of its own on the Mac Studio (2026-10-28). A
    `derive`/`recompute --dry-run` tree, or a `verify --level rederive` tree, in the system temporary directory could
    then not hard-link the source's raw objects (D-32), so every object was copied and re-hashed ("hard links are not
    possible here"; 3,253 objects on `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2`).
  - **Change.** `corpus/scratch.py` `scratch_tree()` makes the private tree under `$AGENTPROV_HOME/tmp` or in the system
    temporary directory, whichever has the source's `st_dev`. A corpus on a third volume, or one that cannot be
    stat'ed, falls back to the system temporary directory and the D-32 copy path, with its existing notice. The tree is
    never inside a corpus, and where it lies changes no output byte.
  - **Other paths checked; none needed a change:**
    - `derive --out` takes the user's NEW;
    - the derive, validate and import scratch stores only put bytes;
    - the importer's temporary AER is read back, never renamed;
    - `package` and the release builder copy no raw objects.
  - **Measured.**
    - `recompute --dry-run --jobs 3` links all 3,253 objects and copies none (before: copies all 3,253). Outputs stay
      identical: 3,243 identical, 0 unexplained.
    - The speed effect is negligible on these corpora:
      - the copy it saves is 49 MB here (223 MB on `agentdojo-upstream-2024-06-rg1`);
      - `RawObjectStore.put` writes cost the same on both volumes (5,000 puts: 7.9–9.9 s on each; fsync bound);
      - the end-to-end runs, taken at load average 26–35 with suites alongside, ranged 181–432 s per arm, too
        noisy to show it.
    - So this is a robustness change: hard links work again, and dry-run I/O stays on the `AGENTPROV_HOME` volume.
  - **Rejected:** a tree beside the source corpus. It would write inside `corpora/`.
  - **Class 0:** `cli/derive.py`, `corpus/verify.py` and `corpus/scratch.py` are outside every stage scope.
- **D-892 (2026-10-28, measured and rejected: the SEC-22 determinism checks stay in the `serial` xdist group; D-401
  unchanged; M5 Ultra performance round 2, item 3; the user's decision, 2026-10-28).**
  - **The idea.**
    - `tests/security/test_sec22_derive_determinism.py` is 214 s of the `serial` group's ~386 s.
    - Per-worker timelines of `-n 24 --dist loadgroup` suites show that group running on one worker for the whole
      suite and finishing last. The other workers end within about 20 s of each other.
    - `docs/reports/suite-perf/baseline.md` lists the file under "own pools", not "load-sensitive".
    - So it was moved into the bounded `pools` groups, with `POOL_FILES` re-measured on the Mac Studio.
  - **Measured.** Three rounds, the commit before against the same tree with the move, `-n 24 --dist loadgroup`,
    loads 18–34:
    - wall time before 504.5 / 470.9 / 461.2 s, after 502.2 / 469.5 / 466.5 s;
    - with the move, `serial` ended at 281–307 s instead of last (368–406 s);
    - but the other workers then finished later: median worker end 369–402 s, against 339–375 s before.
    - Under real load the suite is bound by its total work and by kernel contention, not by its longest group. All
      three runs with the move passed.
  - **Decision.** Rejected: no wall-time gain, and it would have amended the user-approved D-401. `tests/conftest.py`
    is unchanged.
  - **Also rejected (item 3):** `--dist worksteal`. It was 11 % faster (393.5 s against 440.7 s mean, 3 runs each), but
    it ignores the xdist groups: the `serial` tests ran on 10 workers, up to 5 at once.
- **D-893 (2026-10-28, `validate --corpus --jobs N` stages the next batch while the pool runs the current one; M5 Ultra
  performance round 2, item 1b).**
  - **Finding.** The pooled validate (D-413) alternated. The parent read, verified and staged a 256-row batch while the
    pool sat idle, then waited for the pool. At `--jobs` 3–4 the parent averaged ~0.5 CPU, and `--jobs 16` was no
    faster than `--jobs 8`.
  - **Change.** As `derive` does, the next batch is read and staged while a background thread runs the previous batch's
    jobs. Rows are still recorded in index order.
    - Staged inputs are reference-counted, so bytes two batches share are removed only when the last of them is
      recorded.
    - A cache entry stored by one batch can reach the next batch's rows one batch later. It is a hint the job
      re-checks (D-550), so this affects timing only.
  - **Measured** (`ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2`, 3,243 executions, main's code before against after; every report has
    byte-identical rows):

    | Point | Before | After | Change | Conditions |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | `--jobs 8` | 43.5 s | 31.5 s | −28 % | exclusive window, machine CPU 3–5 |
    | `--jobs 16` | 46.7 s | 37.0 s | −21 % | exclusive window |
    | `--jobs 4`, quietest pair | 58.8 s | 35.3 s | −40 % | load 11–13 |

    - The parent's mean CPU rose from 0.59 to 0.95.
    - A `--jobs 4` pair at load 28–32 gave 223.9 s against 101.3 s. One pair was discarded: the "after" run found
      the tier-4 cache cold (see D-894).
  - **Rejected:** more rows per batch with no overlap. It only shortens the barrier.
  - **Class 0:** `corpus/validation.py` is outside every stage scope.
- **D-894 (2026-10-28, a configurable size cap for the tier-4 round-trip cache: `compute.validation_cache_gib`; M5 Ultra
  performance round 2, item 1c; the user chose 32 GiB for the Mac Studio).**
  - **Finding.** The D-550 cache (`$AGENTPROV_HOME/cache/tier4`) is one LRU store capped at 2 GiB (`DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`),
    shared by every command and session on a machine. A miss costs about four times a hit:
    - `recompute --dry-run --jobs 3` on `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2`: 105.7 s warm, 400.9 s with `--no-validation-cache`;
    - a cold run at `--jobs 8`: 199.3 s against 72.4 s warm.
    One large corpus (`agentdojo-upstream-2024-06-rg1`, 18,241 executions) can evict a smaller corpus's entries. During
    round 2, a run right after the large corpus's warm-up spent 1,705 CPU-seconds where a warm run spends about 330.
  - **Change.** The setting `compute.validation_cache_gib` (GiB, 1–4096) caps the cache for every command that uses it.
    - The commands are `validate`, `derive`, `recompute`, `verify --level rederive` and `import`. All of them build it
      through `cli/checks.validation_cache`.
    - Unset, the cache keeps its own 2 GiB default.
    - The cap only bounds the eviction after a run. It never changes an outcome, because a hint is re-checked by the
      job (D-550).
  - **Recommended:** 32 GiB on the Mac Studio (the user's value; its `AGENTPROV_HOME` volume has 1.7 TiB free):
    `agentprov settings set compute.validation_cache_gib 32`. The M2 Max keeps the default.
  - **Not changed:** the built-in default in `validate/cache.py`. That file is in the validation stage scope, so raising
    the default is class 1 and waits for the round-1 seal.
  - **Rejected:**
    - a `--validation-cache-gib` flag on each command: five commands to keep in step for a per-machine fact;
    - an environment variable alone: invisible in `settings list`.
  - **No GUI control.** The reverse-parity rule (D-700) needs every GUI input to be a CLI setting, not the other way.
  - **Class 0:** `cli/checks.py` and `settings.py` are outside every stage scope.
- **D-895 (2026-10-28, `derive`/`recompute` batch size follows the worker count; M5 Ultra performance round 2,
  item 1b).**
  - **Finding** (`recompute --dry-run` on `ast-survey-agentdojo-rg2`, main's code, exclusive window):
    - The derive pool, and the re-map's importer pool, retire every worker at the end of each 256-unit batch.
    - System time grows with worker starts, about 1 s each: 29 s at `--jobs 1`, 86 s at `--jobs 8`, 263 s at
      `--jobs 16`. `--jobs 16` was slower than `--jobs 8` (86.5 s against 72.4 s).
    - A profile of the parent at `--jobs` 3 and 16 shows it saturating one core (mean 0.86–0.87, p90 1.0). The parent
      seals AERs, runs the AER validator, writes and fsyncs each object, and reads cache hints. That sets a floor
      that more workers cannot lower.
  - **Change.** With no explicit batch size, `batch_for(workers)` = 64 units per worker (one worker lifetime), between
    256 and 1024.
    - It sets the re-derive batch, and the re-map's importer batch (`cli/derive._remap`).
    - A batch size never changes an output. Every measured batch size gave 3,243 identical and 0 unexplained. A new
      test compares one unit per batch with the default, byte for byte.
  - **Measured** (exclusive window, machine CPU 4–7):

    | Workers | Batch 256 | Batch 1024 | Batch 4096 |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | 8 | 66.2 s (system 97 s) | 63.0 s (system 58 s) | — |
    | 16 | 79.7 s (system 334 s) | 64.1 s (system 141 s) | 65.5 s (system 102 s) |

    So `--jobs 16` now matches `--jobs 8`. Past that the parent is the limit.
  - **Held as class 1** (until the round-1 seal):
    - workers kept alive across batches (`io/workers.py`);
    - no fsync for a throwaway dry-run tree (`raw/store.py`);
    - AER validation in the worker (`aer/`, `adapters/runner/`).
    These are the levers below the parent's floor.
  - **Not changed:** `validate`'s own 256-row batch (D-893 overlaps it instead; larger batches there are not yet
    measured).
  - **Class 0:** `corpus/derive.py` and `cli/derive.py` are outside every stage scope. The importer is only passed an
    argument it already takes.

The user made the deposit under the existing

- **D-910 (2026-10-28, the datasheet quotes a source's required attribution verbatim; user-approved 2026-10-28 in the
  pre-release-checks session, item 1; `docs/reports/release/pre-release-checks.md` check 8, C-1).** The seal dry run of

  `survey-runs@3` quotes the title of the survey's Zenodo artefact, which contains the word "Reproducible", and the
  datasheet rendered it as AgentPROV text. A third party's title is not an AgentPROV claim.
  - **Decision (as built; revised 2026-10-29, see below):**
    - `corpus/datasheet.py` renders the attribution on one line that starts with the fixed prefix
      `- Required attribution (verbatim): `, each entry in double quotes and escaped for display (`escape_untrusted_line`
      then `escape_markdown`: no line break, no HTML, no inline markup), so an entry can neither end the line nor start a
      second one with the prefix.
    - `adapters/registry/claims.py`: `lint_datasheet` (a generated datasheet only) skips the AR-12 ("reproducible") and
      NC-ALL-03 (scope words) matches on a line that starts with exactly that prefix. Every other rule still applies there,
      and every other line is linted as before. A prefix that is indented, mid-line or not exact exempts nothing.
      `lint_text` without the flag (cards, documents) is unchanged.
    - `lint_card`, which also lints every datasheet statement at sealing, refuses the phrase "Required attribution
      (verbatim)" anywhere (`H.9(4)`): only the renderer may quote third-party text.
  - **Revision (2026-10-29, before any seal).** The first build (`e47258d2`) marked the quoted span with HTML comments
    (`<!-- agentprov:verbatim -->`). The full suite failed `tests/security/test_sec12_display_surfaces.py`: K.12.6(e) and
    F-12C-03 (b) keep `<!--` out of every datasheet, because an HTML comment can hide the rest of the file in a Markdown
    renderer, the "Untrusted content" section included. The markers were replaced by the line prefix, and the
    attribution is now escaped; the invariant holds as written, with no test exception.
  - **Byte class 0, proved:** 41 stage code digests (`aer` and `adapter_code_sha256` per family, `sem` per semantics
    directory, `prov`, `validation`, `compat`) computed with `stage_definitions.code_sha256` at `8c244150` and after the
    change: none moved. Neither file is in a stage scope. Output bytes change only in `DATASHEET.md` of a corpus sealed
    after this lands (no corpus is sealed).
  - **Rejected:** HTML-comment markers (the revision above); a test exception for fixed marker strings (it would weaken
    K.12.6(e)); changing the profile's attribution text (a `survey-runs@4` bump under D-31 and a re-import, to edit a
    third party's title); a general AR-12 exemption for quoted text (a card could then quote its own claim); exempting the
    whole "Distribution and licensing" section (it also renders AgentPROV text: the derived-licence and policy lines).
  - **Tests:** `tests/adapters/registry/test_claims.py` (the exemption; the prefix indented, mid-line or inexact; the card

  decision in the orchestrator window).** The private development repository was renamed `nickjones39/agentprov-framework`

  from a fresh git history. Every sealed corpus records its building commit, and recompute and verify reproduce a

  `git archive` snapshot of that commit (the copyleft test fixtures approved for the private repository are left out)

  building tags (`wave2/build-*`) are pushed to the development repository first. Rejected: (A) making the development
  repository public, and (B) an open full bundle. The history holds account paths and secrets that later commits

- **D-920 (2026-10-29, the release-scan triage writer, C-3; the classes are the user's, approved in the
  pre-release-checks session: items 2 and 6, tables 4b and 4c, check 3 of
  `docs/reports/release/pre-release-checks.md`).**
  After sealing, the 8 round-1 corpora's release scans left their `gitleaks` and `account-path` findings untriaged
  (8,445 in 6 corpora), and the deposit builder refuses an untriaged finding (G.9.4). They were reviewed by class, never
  by value. A triage file lists them by fingerprint, so a tool must turn the class decisions into entries.
  - **Decision (as built):** `tools/release_triage.py` (outside `src/`, like `release_scan.py`):
    - It reads the corpus's untriaged scan document (same root digest, pinned scanners) and runs the pinned gitleaks
      again, redacted, for the key names only. Its fingerprints must equal the document's, or nothing is written.
    - Each `gitleaks` finding gets a class (rule, key name, origin), by check 4b's method. `upstream-data`: a 16+
      character token of the line, or a private-key header, occurs in the benchmark's own suite data (`--suites`).
      `benchmark-input` or `model-generated`: by the AER record's `k` and `role`. A PROV, SEM or raw copy follows its
      execution's AER findings: their one origin; or n-th copy to n-th AER finding when the counts are equal (with the
      key, then the rule alone); or, failing both, n-th copy to n-th AER finding in line order, which is check 4b's own
      rule. Otherwise `unclassified`. When several report entries fall on one line, their key names are joined sorted
      with `+`, since gitleaks' report order is not fixed.
    - Each `account-path` finding gets the ordinals of the account names on its line, numbered by first appearance in
      label order (the post-check's method). Names stay in memory, and no name or digest of one is written.
    - A reviewed decisions file (`agentprov-triage-decisions/0.1`) maps `[[secret]]` classes and `[[account]]`
      ordinals to `synthetic-benchmark`, `model-generated` or `false-positive`, never `real`. Each row carries the count
      its review saw (`findings`, or an ordinal's `hits` by area); any other count writes nothing. A line with several
      ordinals takes the first of their triages in the order model-generated, synthetic-benchmark, false-positive.
    - The output is `<corpus>.release-triage.toml` beside the sealed tree, next to `<corpus>.release-scan.json` (D-609).
      A path inside the tree is refused. The decisions files of round 1 are kept in the repository
      (`docs/reports/release/pre-release-checks/triage-decisions/`): they hold rules, key names, origins, ordinals and
      counts only.
    - `--report` prints the classes and counts that a reviewer needs to write a decisions file. `--list-secrets` prints
      one line per distinct gitleaks value: a 16-hex HMAC-SHA256 under a random per-run key, plus the value's rules,
      keys, origins and counts. The values come from an unredacted gitleaks run read from standard output (never a
      file). `--show` adds them, fenced by `quote_untrusted`, and only when standard output is a terminal.
    - `release_scan.run_gitleaks` and `parse_gitleaks_report` gain the optional `matches` sink and `redact=False` for
      this tool. With their defaults the scan is unchanged.
  - **Reproduction of the approved tables.** On the sealed trees the classes equal table 4b, by rule, origin and layer,
    in all 6 corpora with gitleaks findings, and the ordinals' released hits equal table 4c and the forecast. Joining
    key names moves only the key column: in AgentHarm, 6 class rows have joined keys (such as `encryption_key+key`)
    where the scratch table took the last report entry's key. The first build paired copies only on equal counts.
    That left AgentHarm's 3 PROV findings `unclassified`, where the approved table has `benchmark-input` (a PROV
    document's one line copies findings of both origins). The line-order tier was then added as check 4b states it.
    Item 6 is applied as decided: agentdyn-a's 14 released `password` findings in uncited raw files (`unclassified`)
    are `model-generated`, and ordinal #20 is `false-positive`. Its 2 withheld ones are not in the sealed tree.
  - **Byte class 0, proved:** no file under `src/` changes, and `agentprov.stage_scopes` puts no path under `release/`
    or `tools/` in any stage scope (91 scoped paths, 13 families). No corpus byte changes: the triage files and scan
    documents sit beside the trees.
  - **Rejected:**
    - Joining the pre-seal scratch table to the sealed scan by file digest and line. The table was made on the working
      trees by scratch code. A tool that recomputes the classes on the sealed tree checks the table instead of trusting
      it.
    - Triage entries written by hand per fingerprint (8,445 entries, decided per class anyway).
    - Deciding mixed-origin copies by the strongest disclosure (`model-generated`). It is defensible, but it would
      change 3 findings of a class the user approved. Noted for the next round's review.
    - A digest of each account name to key the ordinals (short names can be brute-forced; pre-check w3-7 used ordinals
      for that reason).
    - Writing the unredacted gitleaks report to a temporary file for `--list-secrets`.
    - C-2 (`release_scan.py --forecast`) in the same change. It needs the seal's withholding plan, which only the
      private `corpus.package._plan` computes. A public plan API in `corpus/` is a change of its own, for the next
      round's pre-release check.
  - **Tests:** `tests/unit/release/test_release_triage_tool.py`, synthetic data only. It covers the origins (suite data,
    record kind, copies paired or in line order, an uncited raw object), key names, ordinals (first appearance,
    trailing dots, allowlisted names, several on a line), refused decision files and counts, the file beside the
    corpus that `release_scan.py --triage` accepts, refusals (inside the tree, another root digest, a stale scanner,
    another gitleaks finding set), and that `--report` and `--list-secrets` print no value without `--show` on a
    terminal.
- **D-930 (2026-10-28, `aprov` catalogue v3: an assessment cites no premise field declared unknown; user-approved
  2026-10-28 in the wave-2 session, "Yes go ahead"; byte class 2, as D-621).** The wave-2 imports of
  `credleak-p15b` · `head` and `dca-agentdojo` · `drift` each sealed one execution as `validate.failed` (tier 3,
  `pv.profiles.unk_premise`, NE-12). In both, a SEM `role` label rests on a `tool_execution`'s `/name` that the mapper
  declared `unk: ambiguous`, and `aprov.a_label@1` cited that field as `apv:sourcePointer`.
  - **The conflict.** SEM-V06 admits a premise declared in the record's `unk` (a label may rest on what the record
    does not know). NE-12 forbids a PROV statement whose field is in `unk`, and E.1.5 item 1 reads such a field as not
    present. The engine's node and edge rules apply E.1.5 item 1 (`Ctx.present`); the assessment rules' `premises()`
    resolved the field with `Ctx.val` and cited it unconditionally. The defect is the engine's, not the labellers'.
  - **Decision.** `aprov.a_label@2`, `aprov.a_payload@2` and `aprov.a_author@2` cite only the premise fields that are
    not declared unknown (`Ctx.unk_reason`, the pointer or an enclosing one). Each field left out is counted as
    `premise_field_unknown` in the assessment counters of the derivation report (E.7.3). The label itself is kept,
    with its SEM class: the claim is SEM's, and its evidence class already follows the SEM `ev` and rules (weakest
    premise, E.1.5 item 2). Premise annotations and the target are unchanged.
  - **Catalogue version 3.** The `aprov` catalogue goes from version 2 to 3. The three @1 rules stay for the documents
    that cite them. Version 2 (`99b6511a2d5e…`, which the eight sealed round-1 corpora and every wave-2 corpus built so
    far record) is archived byte-exact in `prov/catalogue/archive/agentprov-prov-0.1.v2.toml`; `corpus.authority`
    answers v1 and v2 from their archives. `validate.profiles` admits the @2 rules where @1 is admitted; the semdiff
    map targets both versions.
  - **Bytes (class 2).** The catalogue digest enters every bundle's derivation key (E.3.4), so every bundle IRI of a
    derivation at this commit differs from v2's, and every assessment statement of these three rules cites `@2`. No
    stored corpus changes: corpora keep the version they record and are reproduced at their building commit (F-8,
    D-430); a writing `recompute` or `derive` of a v2 corpus here refuses with version drift, so an upgrade is a fresh
    re-import. Pins regenerated: golden PROV, gate D, the DTap SEM/PROV digests and `docs/compat/semantic-diff.md`.
    `prov/compat/adprov_v2_3/` is untouched and its gate passes byte-identical.
  - **Scope of the rebuild (user, 2026-10-28).** Only `credleak-p15b` and `dca-agentdojo` are rebuilt, as new trees
    at this commit. The read-only NE-12 scan of DTap (the other wave-2 corpus whose mapper declares names `unk`) found
    0 of 60,553 executions exposed: its 20,300 `unk` names are claudesdk tool-result names that no label cites.
  - **Manuscript.** Datasheet item 23: under catalogue v3 an assessment never cites a field the record declares
    unknown, and the count of such omitted premises is reported per corpus.
  - **Rejected.**
    - Changing the CredLeak and AgentDojo labellers to stop citing `/name` when it is `unk`: SEM-V06 allows it, and
      every labeller would need the same guard.
    - Dropping the whole statement when one premise field is unknown: the label is SEM's claim and its other premises
      (the target first) still justify it; dropping it would lose a valid label for a citation defect.
    - Editing aprov v2 in place (E.9: a change of a rule's statement mints @n+1, and stored corpora record v2's bytes).
    - Regenerating only the PROV of the affected corpora from their stored AER and SEM: refused by design (D-430).
- **D-931 (2026-10-28, a source profile may raise its `map` jobs' memory cap: `[import] map_rss_bytes`; MCPHunt

  import"; core byte class 0 or 1 by scope, family byte class 1).** The wave-2 import of `mcphunt` · `head` sealed 3 of
  its 35 trace documents whole as `map.adapter_defect` (`worker.limit.rss`), so their 1,254 traces were missing.
  - **Measurement** (read-only, through the queue: the runner's `_job_map_stream` in one process on each failing stored
    object, with the profile's limits and its pinned `hf` origin; sizes and RSS only):
    - `mitigation/minimax_m3_rv1.json` (55 MB, 147 traces, the largest 46.9 MB, a 43.6 MB `result_full`): peak 1,686
      MiB. Phases: `sniff_stream` 33 -> 724 MiB; `parse_stream` to its first item 1,182 MiB; the 46.9 MB trace 1,641 MiB.
    - `main/deepseek_v4_flash.json` (111 MB, 723 traces, the largest 20.5 MB): peak 1,615 MiB.
    - `mitigation/gpt54_m0.json` (43 MB, 384 traces, the largest 25.6 MB): peak 1,322 MiB.
    - The parent's watchdog kills at `cap - margin` (G.4.3). On this host the margin is 163 MiB (the default 4 GiB/s
      allocation rate; D-825 kept it), so the 2 GiB map cap triggers at 1,884 MiB, and these three documents, plus the
      worker's own footprint and frame encoding, cross it. The other 32 documents stay under it.

    profile load) raises the cap of the source's `map` jobs only. The importer carries it on every map job of the import
    (`Job.limits`, which the pool already honours), and the `--size-hints` admission charge reads a job's own limits.
    `mcphunt` declares 4 GiB, 2.4x the measured worst peak. Every other source keeps the default, so its default
    parallelism is unchanged.

    compares the AER bytes. The core change (`adapters/profiles.py`, `runner/importer.py`, `cli/import_.py`) and the
    `mcphunt` profile value are two commits on two branches, because the mcphunt new-family guard keeps a family branch
    off `runner/`; the family branch rests on the core one. The `mcphunt` profile v2 is recorded by the failed wave-2
